title: Remove the middle feeder from a packed feeder rail on a pick-and-place machine
instruction: Take the middle feeder off the rail and lay it on its side on the blue mat. Leave the other two feeders in place.
context: Robot builders assemble their motor-driver and sensor boards on pick-and-place machines such as the desktop LumenPnP; every board change means swapping tape feeders on the machine's front rail. The feeders sit side by side at the rail's 15.8 mm slot pitch, 0.8 mm apart, so no finger fits beside the middle one, and once tipped out of line it drops back into its sprung catch unless held. The machine's leg, side frame and bed limit the approach. A neighbour knocked off its slot loses its place.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the bench top: x forward, y to the robot's left. An Opulo LumenPnP pick-and-place machine stands on the bench to the robot's right, modelled at true size from the maker's assembly CAD: its front frame rail (black 20 x 20 mm V-slot aluminium extrusion) runs along x from 150 to 750 with its centre line at y -70, 110 mm above the bench; its front legs stand at the rail's ends (front left leg x 140-180, y -60 to +44, up to 220 high; front right leg x 720-760), its back frame rail and back legs 440 to 560 mm further right; side frame rails run back from y +20 at x 150-170 and 730-750 (120-140 and 190-218 high); the bed plate (3 mm, 140 high) starts at y -145; the bottom camera sits under it at x 251-289; the control box is on the left side (x 85-150, y -90 to -304, up to 140 high); the gantry is parked at the back (beam at y -480 to -500, 225-265 high, on carriages at both sides; toolhead x 549-639). On the rail's left face stands the yellow slot blade (28 mm deep, 45 mm tall) with one 5 x 5.5 x 6 mm peg per slot. Three Opulo 8 mm tape feeders sit in slots 1 to 3 (front, middle, back at x 261, 276.7, 292.5; 15.8 mm pitch): a black body 15 wide and 165 long, 70 mm in from the rail centre and 95 out, hooked into the slot along the rail's top and clipped round the peg by a yellow two-tooth sprung lever under the blade; each carries on its spool arm a white 7 inch (178 mm) reel, 13 mm wide, hub at y +116 and 95 mm above the bench, turning freely on its hub, with the tape threaded into the feeder. Body 0.13 kg and reel 0.13 kg (estimates). A blue anti-static mat, 300 x 420 x 3 mm, 0.5 kg, lies at (350, 425). Lot B moves the mat to (320, 425). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Drawings: README and fixture/.
scoring: Judged from the videos and photos, with a ruler. 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: either outer feeder is knocked loose, meaning its hook nose leaves the slot in the rail's top face (the nose's lowest point rises above that face, or its axis moves outside the slot's 5 mm width) or its catch lets go (a yellow lever tooth comes out from under the slot blade: the tooth's centre rises above the blade's bottom face, or the whole tooth moves out in front of the blade) or, as a backstop, it moves more than 5 mm at its hook or turns more than 10 degrees; a brief rock within these that leaves it hooked and latched does not count. Also 0 at any moment if any feeder is dropped (its body, at its hook, moving faster than 1.2 m/s, as in a free fall from about 7 cm) or leaves the bench (its hook point 2 cm below the bench top). At the end: 0 if either outer feeder sits more than 2 mm (at its hook) or 3 degrees from where it started, or any part of the middle feeder is within 5 mm of the rail, the slot blade or a peg. 0.5: the middle feeder is 5 mm or more clear of all of them (held, moving, or not lying on a side). 0.75: it also lies on one of its broad sides, within 20 degrees of flat, resting on the bench or mat (lowest point within 5 mm of it), with no gripper within 5 mm, all of this holding with it still (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s) for 1 s. 1.0: as 0.75, and all of it lies inside the mat's outline. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: 1. Lay the mat flat at its lot position (lot A centre (350, 425) mm; lot B (320, 425)). 2. Park the gantry at the back of its travel. 3. Mount each feeder in slots 1 to 3: hold it with the reel end high, set its hook nose into the slot on the rail's top face, swing the reel end down until the clip straddles the peg and the yellow lever clicks under the blade. 4. Check each feeder body rests flat on the rail, the reels hang free 6 mm above the bench, and each reel's tape is threaded and taut. 5. Check with a spring scale that pressing a feeder's inner end down, 60 mm in from the rail centre line, with about 6 N tips it out of its catch (the simulated release force), then reseat it. 6. Move both arms to their rest poses.
fidelity: Machine frame, legs, bed, camera, control box, parked gantry, rail, slot blade, pitch: boxes placed from the maker's CAD; feeder envelope from its CAD. Hook, clip, lever: simplified, sized from photos; they, masses and lever spring are estimates. Reels turn on their hubs with light drag; threaded tape is a one-way stop (can unwind, not wind). Feeder friction 0.38 static (top of the range measured for printed PLA pairs), 0.30 sliding (estimate). No electrical contacts; lots move only the mat.
scores: Demo: A 1.0, B 1.0 (mean 1.0). Dream-1: A 0.0, B 0.0 (both to the 2,400-step limit, middle feeder still seated).
